articles.title: Install a module
articles.summary: The general flow for Magisk, KernelSU and APatch modules.

content.text: Back up your data first and read the module page. Install only modules that list your root solution and Android version as compatible.

items: Download the module ZIP from the Downloads page.
Verify the SHA-256 checksum (see the next article).
Open your root manager app (Magisk, KernelSU or APatch).
Go to the Modules section and choose to install from storage.
Select the ZIP file and wait for the installer to finish.

content.text: Menu names differ between manager versions. The idea stays the same: install the ZIP from the Modules section, then reboot.
If something misbehaves, disable or remove the module from the same Modules screen and reboot. Then collect logs and report the issue.

articles.title: Verify a download
articles.summary: Compare the SHA-256 checksum of your file with the one on the Downloads page.

content.text:
# prints the SHA-256 checksum
sha256sum module.zip
The printed value must match the checksum shown next to the download exactly. If it does not, delete the file and download it again.

articles.title: Collect logs with adb
articles.summary: Capture the information needed to diagnose a problem.

content.text: Connect the device with USB debugging enabled, then run:

adb devices
adb logcat -d > logcat.txt
adb shell getprop ro.build.fingerprint
Logs can contain personal data such as account names and device identifiers. Review the file and remove anything private before sharing it.

articles.title: Report an issue
articles.summary: What to include so a problem can be reproduced.

items: Root solution and its version (Magisk, KernelSU or APatch)
Module or project name and version
What you expected and what happened instead
A log file, if the problem involves a crash or boot issue

content.text: Open the issue in the GitHub repository of the project concerned. One problem per issue keeps the discussion easy to follow.
